text_copy: AUDIT/primary/fechner2022-bfr-meal-hg-cd-pb-ni-germany.txt (PDF); AUDIT/primary/fechner2022-bfr-meal-hg-cd-pb-ni-germany-mmc2.tsv (all sheets of mmc2.xlsx, parsed from XML); AUDIT/primary/fechner2022-bfr-meal-hg-cd-pb-ni-germany-mmc1.txt (Text S1, Tables S1-S2)
disposition_reason: German total diet study (BfR MEAL) reporting tHg, Cd, Pb and Ni in one pooled sample each of cocoa powder, instant cocoa beverage powder and dark chocolate, and in organic and conventional milk chocolate pools (Tables S3-S6). Cocoa powder had the highest Ni in the study and among the highest Cd and Pb.
disposition_locator: mmc2.xlsx Tables S3-S6 rows R559, R566, R567, R638, R639; main text 3.1.1-3.1.3 and 3.3.4

study.material_scope: retail cocoa powder, instant cocoa beverage powder, dark chocolate, milk chocolate (organic and conventional pools); no white chocolate pool
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Purchase market Germany (national foods sampled in the Berlin area; production-type pools organic purchased in Berlin area). Growing origin of cocoa not reported; authors speculate origin explains differences versus other TDSs.
study.collection_period: Purchasing 2017-2019 per paper (BfR Communication 033/2022 on the same pools states December 2016 to May 2019); per-pool purchase dates not given.
study.sampling_unit: pooled composite samples: 20 subsamples (national pools) or 15 subsamples (organic/conventional milk chocolate pools); 1 pool per food/stratum
study.method: tHg: direct mercury analyser (DMA-80, thermal decomposition-amalgamation AAS); Cd, Pb, Ni: microwave digestion (HNO3/H2O2, DIN EN 13805) + ICP-MS, duplicate analysis; homogenised with titanium knives/polypropylene to avoid Ni contamination
study.lod_loq: Table S2 (mg/kg) moist/dry foods: Cd LOD 0.0003/0.002, LOQ 0.001/0.005; Pb LOD 0.001/0.001, LOQ 0.002/0.004; Hg LOD 0.001/0.003, LOQ 0.002/0.005; Ni LOD 0.006/0.03, LOQ 0.02/0.1. Hg LOD/LOQ raised mathematically for samples diluted with water during homogenisation.
study.basis: Chocolates: as consumed (= as purchased). Cocoa powder and instant cocoa beverage powder: unprepared dry powder as sold (prep code d), NOT as the beverage.
study.qa: Accredited contract laboratories; CRM NIST 1573a tomato leaves (Hg, every 10 samples) and NIST 1849 milk powder (Cd/Pb/Ni each run); blanks; expanded measurement uncertainty 20% (Cd, Pb, Ni), 30% (Hg). Recoveries not reported.

findings.locator: mmc2.xlsx sheet S3_Mercury_Hg (Table S3) row R559
findings.notes: One pooled sample of 20 retail subsamples (BfR MEAL TDS; type "N"). preparation code a: "only subsamples ready prepared for consumption" (chocolate eaten as purchased; no further preparation described). Value is the arithmetic mean of duplicate analyses of the pool. Tables S2 LOD/LOQ (mg/kg): moist LOD 0.001/LOQ 0.002; dry LOD 0.003/LOQ 0.005; which class applied to this pool is not stated. Result non-quantified: mLB 0 (i.e. below LOD), UB 0.004101655601058954 mg/kg (= substituted LOD per UB rule). Main text cites this pool as UB mean.
findings.integrity_issue: UB substitute 0.004102 mg/kg equals neither the moist (0.001) nor dry (0.003) Hg LOD in Table S2 although mLB=0 implies all results <LOD; possibly a pool-specific LOD (Text S1: Hg LOD/LOQ raised mathematically for water-diluted samples) averaged over duplicate analyses. Not reconcilable from the source.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary calls cocoa powder Cd 0.270 mg/kg the "joint highest Cd in study"; boletus/porcini mushroom had 0.320 mg/kg (main text 3.1.2), so cocoa powder is second.
Stored summary omits the milk chocolate pools (organic Cd 0.056 vs conventional 0.016 mg/kg; Ni 0.825 vs 0.700) and the instant cocoa beverage powder Cd/Pb values (0.0305/0.0155 mg/kg).
Stored summary does not state that cocoa powder and cocoa beverage powder were analysed unprepared (dry powder), which the paper states explicitly.
Stored summary sample_population says foods purchased 2017-2019; the companion BfR Ni communication says December 2016-May 2019 for the same pools.
unresolved: Whether moist- or dry-food LOD/LOQ applied to chocolates is not stated; Hg UB substitutes for dark/milk chocolate (0.0039-0.0041 mg/kg) and instant cocoa beverage powder (0.0033 mg/kg) do not match either tabulated LOD although mLB=0 (flagged integrity_issue).
Cocoa content, cocoa percentage and growing origin of the pooled chocolates and powders are not reported.
Exact purchase dates per pool not given; years recorded as the full 2016-2019 purchase window.
